Every thesomid, a newly described family.why: The thesomids are made up: a family of spiders of that name does not exist, and no text states this. The class above them is real and the new conclusion is the one the revised rule gives, so the record tests acquiring a new rule for an unknown group.

Orlu has six legs..why: Made up, so stated nowhere: nobody writes a fact about an animal that does not exist. It follows only from the inserted rule and the membership given in the prompt (the individual is named as a thesomid), which is how people state things about a member of a group: through its group.

A thesomid has the same number of legs a.why: Nobody compares the leg count of a made-up family with that of ants. What people do say is that ants have six legs; the comparison follows only from the inserted rule and that fact.

notes: TBox expansion paired with biology-replace-0005 (spider legs: eight to six): keeps the revision's relation and new object (six legs) and gives it to a made-up family of spiders (the thesomids) under the real class, so the old value has nothing to push out. Own questions ask the new value; the propositional side facts are one true and one false. Derived: an inheritance question and an application that name a member in the prompt, and a composition that compares with a fact stored about ants (derivation none). Unrelated near: a wolf spider's legs (eight), so a leak of the rule onto real members would change it. Known weakness: a six-legged spider family contradicts the inherited rule that spiders have eight legs, so the model has to override its superclass.
